correctness.rationale: A full symbolic sweep derivation on matching pairs and unmatched sites establishes an invertible coordinate change (pair sums, corrected first endpoints, zero-sum shift coordinates). It splits the update into a cyclic shift on a length-(n-2k+1) zero-sum space and a square-zero shear I+J_k. Since n is even, this shift length is odd and the fixed space of its tth power has dimension gcd(n-2k+1,t)-1. The shear rank is exactly k for even k and k-1 for odd k, including k=0,1 boundaries. These give the actual maximal periods and all q-ary fixed-state counts; Möbius inversion yields primitive-orbit counts. The code paths code/verify_scan.py and code/verify_direct.cpp were executed, respectively confirming 7,728 and 757,296 GF(2) labelled cases. Finite checks corroborate, and do not replace, the unrestricted characteristic-two proof.

value.rationale: Deleting two disjoint edges from an even complete graph changes a sequential local-parity map from a shift of maximal period n+1 to a direct sum with a nonzero square-zero shear and maximal period 2(n-3), despite deletion of only two of n(n-1)/2 edges. This reverses the effect of one deleted edge (period n-1) for every even n>=8. The proved all-k, all-characteristic-two structural similarity and exact primitive orbit populations give a motivated, extensible answer about perturbation sensitivity of sequential network dynamics, not a routine isolated numerical count.
